daily_summary.html:
Domestic Politics

PDI-P Secretary General Hasto Kristiyanto announced the death of Guruh Soekarnoputra, the youngest son of founding president Soekarno and younger brother of former president Megawati Soekarnoputri, at age 73. The party remembered Guruh as a great artist, Marhaenist, and party fighter, highlighting his decades-long contributions to Indonesian arts and politics. Mourners began arriving at the funeral home to pay respects to the renowned musician and former legislator.

  • The Corruption Eradication Commission (KPK) named the Gowa regent a corruption suspect for allegedly demanding money from developers and minimarket chains, with police pledging no interference despite the suspect being the sibling of National Police Chief Fadil Imran.
  • The Minister of Immigration and Correctional Facilities conducted an inspection of Cibinong Prison following allegations of luxury facilities, finding some furniture already removed, and promised a full investigation into the scandal.
  • Former President Jokowi continued his political tour to Bandung and Bekasi alongside the Indonesian Solidarity Party (PSI).
  • A Constitutional Court judge questioned why the General Elections Commission (KPU) uses different methods to verify diplomas for regional elections versus presidential elections.
  • The Banyumas district secretary submitted his resignation after being questioned by the KPK.
  • A DPR member from Central Kalimantan explained that residents have not recovered from the impacts of recent forest and land fires.
  • A legislator confirmed that the Jabodetabek odd-even traffic policy ran optimally as the measure concluded.

Foreign Policy & Defence

Indonesia's delegation walked out of the UN General Assembly during Israeli Prime Minister Netanyahu's speech, joining 70 countries in the protest, with the Foreign Ministry describing the walkout as a form of solidarity for Palestine. At the UN forum, Indonesia pledged $1.2 million to the UN Relief and Works Agency for Palestinian refugees and called on the Organisation of Islamic Cooperation to unite in support of Palestinian independence.

  • Indonesia's Foreign Minister highlighted Indonesia's peace experiences in Aceh and Maluku at a UN forum and called for faster implementation of a two-state solution to the Israeli-Palestinian conflict.
  • Indonesia reaffirmed its commitment to ocean-climate action at a UN meeting and showcased its giant sea wall and mangrove rehabilitation projects at the same forum.
  • Indonesia proposed nearly 24 million hectares of new Marine Protected Areas as part of its environmental commitments.
  • Defence Minister Prabowo Subianto visited the Talaga Manggung Infantry Battalion and emphasized discipline among soldiers.
  • TNI's Information Chief stated that disputed land in Menteng has the legal status of state property.

Other

Coordinating Minister for Economic Affairs Airlangga Hartarto urged the furniture industry to reduce dependence on US exports and diversify markets. Separately, the government highlighted its US trade agreement as a key investment opportunity for potential investors. Meanwhile, Bank Jakarta and PT SMI disbursed Rp 2.11 trillion to finance seven infrastructure projects.

  • The government will restore the fire-damaged National Museum with the help of state holding company Danantara, with a minister calling museums engines of cultural economy.
  • President Prabowo stated that ground crews are most effective in battling forest fires, while the National Disaster Management Agency chief apologized after saying conditions for fire-affected communities were running normally.
  • The Deputy Environment Minister asked local governments to allocate 3% of regional budgets for waste management.
  • Indonesia and the Japan International Cooperation Agency (JICA) developed a balanced nutrition pilot program based on Japan's food education approach.
  • Vice President Gibran expressed condolences to families of flash flood victims in Solok, West Sumatra.
